paragraphs.text: Listening activity.
Hello, my name is Susan Lee.
I'm a new reporter from the Los Angeles Gazette.
I just started working for the paper last week.
I worked for the Los Angeles News for five years,
but then they closed the newspaper offices.
Good morning, Miss Lee.
I'm writing an article about the Chumash reservation.
Can I ask you a few questions?
Yes, please sit down.
My Chumash name is Wild Wolf,
and I'm the chief of the reservation.
How long have you lived here?
I've lived here all my life, 75 years.
I was born on this reservation,
and my father was born here too.
That's a long time.
Then you know all about the reservation.
This land belonged to your ancestors, didn't it?
Yes, it did, for hundreds of years.
At the end of the 19th century, we lost all our land,
and the American government gave us this reservation in February 1901.
How many people live here?
Only 520 men, women, and children live here today.
But many years ago, more than a thousand people lived here.
Did they go away?
Yes, they went to live in the big city,
because there was little work on the reservation.
At first, they had many big problems.
They couldn't find a place to live, and they couldn't find work.
It was very difficult for them to make friends outside the reservation.
Now, most of them have a home and a job.
What business do you have on the reservation today?
Our only business today is the writing stable.
Do you ever go to Los Angeles?
I only go to Los Angeles once a year in April.
For the big meeting of all the California tribes, the pow-wow.
How interesting!
Do you still work?
Of course I do.
I work at the museum and the gift shop every day of the week,
except Monday, from 10 to 4.
Then I go to the writing stable and help George with the horses and the writing lessons.
A lot of people from Portola Point and other towns come to our stables to learn how to ride.
I like helping George.
He's a good man.
You're a very busy man.
Thank you for the interview, wild wolf.
You're welcome.
Please stay for lunch, Susan.
We're having fish and salad today.
After lunch, you can take pictures of the reservation and visit the stables.
